items.name: Kashmiri chili
items.prabhava: The color chili — deep red with gentle heat; lets a dish look fiery while staying pitta-survivable.
combinations: bloomed in hot oil or ghee for color
contraindications: high pitta (still a chili, just gentler)
items.preparation: Bloom the powder briefly in fat off the highest heat — color releases, bitterness doesn't.

items.name: Byadgi chili
items.prabhava: Karnataka's wrinkled color chili — the Southern counterpart of Kashmiri mirch; deep red, mild fire, signature of Udupi and coastal sambars.
items.preparation: Dry-roast whole pods gently before grinding into spice blends; prized for color over heat.

items.name: Long pepper root
items.prabhava: The root of pippali holds its own place in classical pharmacology — a stronger deepana (agni-kindler) than the fruit, used in pinch doses.
items.preparation: Culinary-medicinal boundary item: pinch doses in spice blends; stronger and drier than pippali fruit.

items.name: Cassia bark
items.prabhava: The thick bazaar 'cinnamon' of Indian groceries — stronger and harsher than true Ceylon cinnamon, with a coumarin load that argues for moderation.
combinations: whole bark in biryanis and stocks (removed before serving)
contraindications: daily heavy use (coumarin — liver caution; prefer Ceylon cinnamon for daily)
items.preparation: Use whole pieces in slow cooking and remove; reserve ground daily-use cinnamon for the true (Ceylon) kind.
provenance: Bazaar tvak convention; modern coumarin evidence

items.name: Bay leaf (Mediterranean)
items.prabhava: True laurel of European kitchens — sharper and more resinous than Indian tej patta; one leaf steers a whole pot.
combinations: soups, stocks and braises (removed before serving)
contraindications: remove before serving (the stiff leaf is a physical hazard)
items.preparation: Simmer whole and fish out; distinct from Indian tej patta (see dravya.bay-leaf) — the two aren't interchangeable in flavor.

items.name: Sage
items.prabhava: The Western drying herb — checks excess secretions (sweat, phlegm) and cuts fatty heaviness; classic partner to rich winter food.
combinations: with squash, beans and rich gravies
browned in ghee or butter over pasta
items.preparation: Fry leaves briefly in fat to mellow the camphor edge; a strongly drying herb — dose like medicine, not salad.

items.name: Marjoram
items.prabhava: Oregano's gentle sibling — the calmer, sweeter herb for the same dishes; mildly settling to digestion and nerves.
combinations: added near the end (gentler than oregano)
items.preparation: Add in the last minutes of cooking; where oregano shouts, marjoram speaks.

items.name: Vanilla
items.prabhava: The comforting aroma — softens and rounds sweet dishes; sattvic in effect, calming rather than stimulating.
combinations: real bean or extract over synthetic vanillin
items.preparation: Split and scrape the bean into warm (not boiling) milk or cream; alcohol-based extract added off the heat.

items.name: Dried mint
items.prabhava: Mint concentrated by drying — keeps the cooling digestion of fresh mint in shelf-stable form; the raita and chaat sprinkle.
combinations: crushed over raitas and dahi preparations
items.preparation: Crush between palms over the finished dish — brief heat, or none, keeps its lift.

items.name: Curry leaf powder
items.prabhava: Dried curry leaves ground with dal and spices — South India's way of eating curry leaf by the spoonful instead of picking it off the plate.
combinations: mixed into hot rice with ghee or til oil
items.preparation: Store-bought or home-ground with roasted dals, chilies and salt; a spoon with ghee rice delivers the leaf's traditional hair-blood-sugar virtues as food.
provenance: South Indian podi tradition; surabhinimba lineage

items.name: Idli podi (gunpowder)
items.prabhava: Roasted urad-chana-chili-sesame powder — the fiery companion of idli and dosa, eaten stirred into ghee or til oil.
combinations: with hot idli and ghee/gingelly oil
items.preparation: Always moistened with ghee or oil — the fat carries flavor and buffers the chili; dry podi scratches vata.

items.name: Mustard powder
items.prabhava: Ground mustard's enzymatic fire — wet-mixed and rested, it develops the sinus-clearing sharpness whole seeds keep hidden.
combinations: a pinch in kadhi and dals
items.preparation: Mix with cool water and rest 10 minutes for full pungency; heat tames it back down.

items.name: Pickle masala
items.prabhava: The North Indian pickling blend — fennel, fenugreek, kalonji, mustard and chili in mustard oil; preservation chemistry as flavor.
combinations: a pinch to give any sabzi 'achari' character
contraindications: hypertension (the salt that travels with it)
items.preparation: Bloom briefly in hot mustard oil before adding vegetables; the whole-seed crunch is traditional.

items.name: Buttermilk masala
items.prabhava: Roasted cumin, black salt, dried mint and ginger — the blend that turns plain chaas into takra proper.
items.preparation: A quarter teaspoon per glass of diluted buttermilk; roast-and-grind fresh monthly for aroma.

items.name: Thandai masala
items.prabhava: The dry form of the festival cooler — almond, melon seeds, fennel, poppy, rose, cardamom, pepper; a cooling-tonic formula in powder.
items.preparation: Two spoons per glass of milk, soaked 10 minutes and strained or drunk whole; grind fresh each spring.
provenance: North Indian festival tradition; char magaz formula

items.name: Hingvastak churna
items.prabhava: The classical eight-ingredient digestive — trikatu, ajwain, both cumins, hing and rock salt; the formula for vata-type gas and heaviness, taken in the first bite of food.
combinations: a pinch mixed with ghee in the first morsel of rice (classical method)
items.preparation: Classical dose is a small pinch with ghee at the start of the meal; a formula on the food-medicine boundary — respect the dose.

items.name: Red amaranth greens (lal chaulai)
items.prabhava: The red-stemmed amaranth — iron-visible in its color; classical marisha with the blood-affinity the pigment suggests.
combinations: Bengali lal shaak with mustard oil
items.preparation: Quick-cook with a little fat; the red bleeds beautifully into dals and rice.
items.reviewNote: Generic amaranth greens exist as dravya.amaranth-leaves (batch 06); this is the red varietal. Green varietal predraft skipped as duplicate.

items.name: Bathua (chenopodium)
items.prabhava: Vastuka is among the most praised greens of classical texts — tridoshic, laxative-gentle and digestible; winter's wild spinach of North India.
items.preparation: Blanch and fold into raita, saag or dough; a winter green worth seeking out — classical texts rank it above most.

items.name: Colocasia leaf (arbi patta)
items.prabhava: The heart-shaped leaf of patra/patrode — always cooked with sour and spice, whose chemistry disarms the leaf's oxalate itch.
combinations: patra: leaves layered with tamarind-besan paste, steamed and sliced
contraindications: must be thoroughly cooked with souring agents (raw oxalate irritation)
items.preparation: Devein, layer with spiced sour besan paste, steam well, then slice and temper — the monsoon delicacy done safely.
items.reviewNote: Canon tender-taro vpk [1, 0, 0] differs from the retained target [1, 0, 1].

items.name: Drumstick leaf (fresh)
items.prabhava: The most nutrient-dense common leaf of the subcontinent — shigru patra warms, scrapes kapha, and carries iron-calcium density that modern analysis confirms.
contraindications: high pitta with heat symptoms (regular large use)
pregnancy (leaf in food amounts fine; bark/root not)
items.preparation: Strip leaflets, cook briefly with dal or coconut; slight bitterness mellows with ghee.

items.name: Gongura (sorrel leaves)
items.prabhava: Andhra's sour signature — the tangiest common leaf; gongura pachadi wakes agni like nothing else on the thali.
combinations: gongura pachadi (chutney) with rice and ghee
with red chili and garlic (traditional pairing)
items.preparation: Cook the leaves down before grinding — their sourness concentrates; ghee on the rice is the traditional buffer.

items.name: Water spinach (kalmi)
items.prabhava: The hollow-stemmed water green of eastern wetlands — cooling, moistening, quick-growing; kalambi appears in regional nighantu lists.
combinations: kalmi saag with garlic and mustard oil (Bengali)
stir-fried on high heat (Southeast Asian style)
contraindications: always cook — raw wetland greens can carry parasites (Fasciolopsis)
items.preparation: High-heat stir-fry with garlic; never raw — the wetland habitat makes thorough cooking non-negotiable.
provenance: Bengali-Assamese tradition; kalambi in regional lists
